kinds.acd_description: Comparisons with regular sound correspondences and close semantics, reconstructed at one level of the ACD tree.
kinds.note: The reconstruction and its reflexes; links are compiled from the ACD tree and marked implied.

kinds.category: cognate set, not a main entry
kinds.acd_description: No description in the release; these sets sit under an etymon beside its main entry (affixed or compound forms such as *ma-m-atay under *atay).
kinds.note: As a cognate set. How a sub-entry relates to its main entry (a derivation from it?) is not documented: listed for acd-2.

kinds.acd_description: Groups the reconstructions of one etymon at its successive levels.
kinds.note: Reconstructions of one etymon at successive levels link to each other, compiled from the tree.

kinds.acd_description: A set of variants that are independently supported by the comparative evidence.
kinds.note: Variants of one word, both endorsed; not competitors.

kinds.acd_description: Variants supported only by allowing the overlap of cognate sets; only one can be consistent with the evidence, but it is unclear which.
kinds.note: One holder, Blust; never counted twice.

kinds.acd_description: Boolean flag on a form's membership in a cognate set.
kinds.wety_kind: certainty on a membership link: possible
kinds.note: Never true in v2.0.

kinds.acd_description: Flag indicating (un)certainty of the reconstruction.
kinds.note: Never set in v2.0.

kinds.acd_description: Proto-forms are often marked as somewhat doubtful (a "?" before the form).
kinds.note: Never true in v2.0.

kinds.acd_description: No column; the gloss of the reconstruction ends in "(?)", as in PWMP *andap 'phosphorescent centipede (?)'.
kinds.wety_kind: form or sense: the sense is doubtful
kinds.note: An attribute of the reconstruction's gloss; it does not lower the link.

kinds.acd_description: A process of metathesis is assumed, explaining the apparent irregularity of a cognate.
kinds.note: Kept under the ACD's name on the membership link; shown, not followed differently.

kinds.acd_description: A process of assimilation is assumed, explaining the apparent irregularity of a cognate.
kinds.note: As Metathesis.

kinds.acd_description: The form differs from the expected reflex, and a copying mistake has not occurred.
kinds.note: Never true in v2.0.

kinds.acd_description: The form is a loanword.
kinds.note: The form is not a reflex; with BorrowingTable below.

kinds.acd_description: CLDF BorrowingTable: a borrowed form, in a loan group (Cfset_ID); no source form is given.
kinds.note: Source_Form_ID is empty in all 7348 rows; the comment may name the donor.

kinds.acd_description: Widely distributed loanwords that could be mistaken for native forms.
kinds.note: A group of borrowed forms; no reconstruction is endorsed.

kinds.acd_description: Chance resemblances, considered and rejected.
kinds.note: Stance rejects; no unnamed ancestor.

kinds.acd_description: Forms that appear to be historically related but are irregular, and do not yet permit a reconstruction.
kinds.note: An unnamed ancestor at "possible" when the members share no named one.

kinds.acd_description: Submorphemic sound-meaning associations (Brandstetter's Wurzeln), not assigned to a proto-language.
kinds.note: Shown, never followed.

kinds.acd_description: Forms related to a cognate set that show some irregularity, given as context.
kinds.note: Shown with the set it names (Cognateset_ID).

kinds.acd_description: A corresponding (unsupported) reconstruction posited in Dempwolff 1938.
kinds.note: Held by Dempwolff 1938; the ACD reports it as unsupported.

kinds.acd_description: The assumed internal classification: the ACD's reconstruction levels.
kinds.note: Recorded with the source; compiled links follow it and are flagged where it differs from Wiktionary's.

kinds.acd_description: The source dictionaries a form or a cognate judgement is taken from.
kinds.note: Forms cite the dictionary they come from; not credits for the etymology.

kinds.acd_description: Who is cited for a cognate set.
kinds.note: Count of sets that cite anyone.

kinds.acd_description: Prose notes: arguments, further comparisons, attributions.
kinds.note: Prose: model extraction (syn-2) may read them; until then shown as notes.
